messages:
ana: Hey team — customer (AcmeSearch) is hitting sporadic 429s on /v1/embeddings during large nightly jobs. They say most failures correlate with a client-side staircase ramp (concurrent workers scaling 1->40 over 90s). Also seeing occasional "dimension mismatch" logged from their client when it retries.
liam: Thanks Ana. Do we have request traces or example payloads? batch_size, model, dims?
maria: I can pull logs. Can someone paste a failing example curl or the error body they see?
ana: (correction) that was me, ana. Example from them:
ana: ```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": 429,
    "message": "rate limit exceeded",
    "retry_after": 5
  },
  "request_id": "req_9f8a3b"
}
```
ana: They use model "embed-large-v1", batch_size=64, input_count=64, expected_dim=1536. Client retry uses fixed 1s backoff for first 3 tries.
liam: Fixed 1s backoff + client staircasing -> likely synchronized bursts causing per-project token QPS cap to trip. Are these Hosted or Dedicated customers?
ana: Hosted.
maria: Pulling ingress rate metrics for AcmeSearch now (project_id: proj_834). Give me 30s.
maria: Found short spike: 38 concurrent connections at t=2370012000, sustained for ~2min. Ratecap window shows several 429s and a queued/drop spike on our edge.
rick: Important: embedding units are charged per input vector attempt. If they retry immediately, that can double request rate and push over burst limit. Also dimension mismatch could come from mixing model variants (older client sending 1024-dims tag?)
liam: Request body sample from their SDK?
ana: They pasted snippet:
ana: ```js
const resp = await client.embeddings.create({
  model: 'embed-large-v1',
  input: docsBatch,
  batch_size: 64
});
```
ana: docsBatch is an array of strings, sometimes empty strings slip in, and their post-processing expects 1536 dims. When retry returns an error body, they sometimes parse partial payloads and assert dims -> dimension mismatch on their side.
maria: So two separate issues: server-side 429s from burst + client-side parsing assumptions causing "dimension mismatch" noise. Need to confirm server didn't return partial vectors.
rick: Can we correlate request_id req_9f8a3b to edge logs and see full response body returns? If the server returned 429, there should be no vector payload.
maria: Confirmed: for req_9f8a3b server returned only 429 JSON. Client attempted to parse as embeddings array and threw dimension error. So mis-handled client error path.
liam: Action items: 1) Recommend client change: implement randomized exponential backoff with jitter and max concurrency cap (e.g., max_workers=8 for large batch jobs). 2) Support: provide repro checklist and short-term mitigation on our side (soft throttle window increase?)
ana: Customer asked if we can temporarily raise burst cap for proj_834 for tonight's nightly job.
rick: We can do an emergency soft lift (tenant-level burst allowance) for 1 hour but need approval and note billing implications.
liam: Also suggest they reduce batch_size to 32 and add client-side validation: only parse embeddings when HTTP 200 and content-type json and embeddings.length == inputs.length.
maria: I'll open a quick ops ticket to increase burst allowance by 2x for 60 minutes starting 2370015600. Also adding a short-lived rule to prefer queueing instead of immediate 429 for this project if possible.
ana: Can you paste the exact repro steps I can give the customer?
maria: Repro checklist (copy to customer):
1) Use a worker harness that ramp-concurrency 1->40 over 90s.
2) Send batches of 64 inputs to POST /v1/embeddings using model=embed-large-v1.
3) Ensure retry policy is fixed backoff 1s (to reproduce sync burst).
4) Observe 429s in ~30-120s window. Collect request_id headers.
5) If client parses on 429 path you may see dimension mismatch errors locally.

Example curl (single batch):
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-large-v1","input":["a","b", ... 64 items]}'
```

Expected failure body on 429:```json
{"error":{"code":429,"message":"rate limit exceeded","retry_after":5},"request_id":"..."}
```

Mitigations: reduce batch_size to 32, add exponential backoff with jitter, cap concurrency, add server-side retry-after header handling before parsing payload.
maria: I'll also add a dashboard short-term showing per-project QPS and burst headroom and pin it for support on-call.
liam: For long-term: we should update docs and SDK templates to include recommended backoff (exp backoff + jitter) and a sample concurrency cap for bulk embedding jobs.
rick: I'll approve the 60min soft lift once billing confirms no auto-escalation. @escalation-bot start billing-check proj_834
escalation-bot: billing-check started for proj_834 — ETA 10m
ana: Thanks all — I'll send the repro checklist + temporary mitigation steps to the customer and ask them to pause overnight jobs until we apply soft lift.
liam: Please request their SDK version and whether they use our official client. If unofficial, send them the suggested snippet to guard parse path.
maria: Logged ops ticket OPS-1287 and scheduled the soft-lift job. Will update when complete.
rick: After soft lift, monitor for repeated synchronous retries; if still trigger, we'll require them to adopt client cap or we'll throttle more aggressively.
ana: Closing loop: will update thread with customer confirmation. :thumbsup:
